### 2026-10-19 – # Made the Schematic

**6.1h**

# Made the Schematic

## Wanted to make a speaker
Was researching what I could make for quite a while, as I was looking into making some sort of sound system, as the speakers themselves seemed a reasonable price for a decent quality.

![9231](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8df2209a10c634a3bbaa1575fd361aa5cfe1806e568c626ba0882e2b202a9411.png)

But the problem was, from my research, I found that speakers are highly dependent on their cases for sound, and without a 3D printer, not much I could do for that, as I can only order things. So annoyingly I had to scrap those 2 hours, and put the time into something else.

## Came up with current idea
So for my tech GCSE, we're going along the idea of multi use tech. So I was thinking to make a Sound Pad, which can function as an instrument, but also possibly behave as a synth/macro pad style thing.
So I researched a bit for the BOM for that, to see if it would be feasible, and I think it will be - and I'm planning to still add a speaker from me research from before - it would likely just be cheaper and not sound half as good.

![9262](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/30a56fc59fd5d1e863135e7fbd65ed9884fe76b4f5e0c088a74d9bb2e4124b6d.png)

Also I was originally planning to go with an ESP32, as I'm fairly experienced in using them, but looking at it, raspberry pi boards have much better community support, especially for this kind of thing, so I decided to give an rp2040 zero a go. I hope this doesn't come back to bite me in the build week when I do the code for it lol.

![9264](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/1c8d4e312ff0efc8bd22ded777a138a890b251d3c242c9df07c4ebf0e82a3168.jpg)

 I also had the problem for what parts to use, as there are many different types of parts..Take keyboard switches for example, there are loads of them, at varying price points, which theoretically all work. I decided to go with the outemu red keyboard switches as they seemed decent, and quite cheap.

But then there's also other decisions like keycaps etc, so I basically went for the most average looking ones I could.

![9255](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/34a8b80b3788a433cf6ff22ddee6d60201b824b9fabc3f8c933204ed344195be.png)

The other thing that was time consuming, as when I looked for rotary encoders originally, there were loads of options - smooth, detents, push button etc, but we're all really expensive. So after researching a lot, I found you can get rotary encoders called ec11's which can be found cheaply and have the appropriate functions.

![9653](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/e88e09683f3fddf94420df0927509705ac7da09e832f33e5f18a1e54638c44ac.png)

## Made the Schematic

So first off, I wasn't planning to make a custom PCB, but it seems you need one for keyboard switches, so I gave in - but it took way longer than I would have liked.

So I'd assumed making the schematic would be simple - as whilst I only learnt how to make them two weeks ago, they seem fairly simple, at least for this little components. And it was, except finding a MX switch symbol and footprint I was happy with was an absolute pain.

![9263](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/a69bb63d78c5f1cffdfcd741f35dc97c3dedd1428d0c1f4fc554d2a2e72f541e.jpg)

So you'd think that something that simple there would be plenty of community contributed designs (I'm working in EasyEDA) - but that was the problem. There were too many designs essentially flooding it with symbols - most of them had no footprint associated.

But in the end, I managed to scrape together the start of a schematic:

![9232](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/30d89711de742bd7ad7a2bced3c2045378ad3840b5af73dae844e753582e860e.png)

And after that, I thought it looked a bit simple, so I decided to add some other things - namely two rotary encoders and a screen - and I've attached them on headers, so I can angle them in the case instead of having them on the PCB.

![9233](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/b4441d4681855a048693d9511b1909c08080677f72a79fdb472bcbbfc74c0dfc.png)

## Next steps
- Layout and route the PCB
- Probably make a case. will see how I'm doing time wise.

## tl;Dr
Spent too long researching parts and compatibility - was probably worth it though. And created the Schematic for the board

### 2026-10-19 – # Routed the board

**5.3h**

# Routed the board

So I finished the schematic earlier today (I've got loads of time, as no school this week), and now I'm thinking of manually routing the PCB. I don't know how hard it is, but I think it will be a fun thing to do.

So I opened it, then had the problem of how to lay out the keyboard switches.

![9234](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/e76a4275919b20997f747cb90e6d16ee0175d7b9f115cd9c99e0b6b82bfb1769.png)

The problem is, keyboard switches are all the same size, but the keycaps are different. So I did a bit of research, and found the distance you're meant to put us 19.05. idk why it's .05, but I did it anyway. And the other problem I had was how many switches to use, and how I wanted to lay them out. Especially in relation to the MCU. But eventually I decided to go with a 2 row of 4 keys design, with the rotary encoders and screen above the MCU.

![9235](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/9e367977dc023102e5754d3f85301c9a4db0ef09fedf578cc089cb5e699b737c.png)

And as I'm planning on not putting those on the PCB, as I plan to make a custom case which should mount those at an angle, I had to add the layouts for the pin headers spaces which I can solder them to.

![9236](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/37b8157f116a5ca75005c82f7a8a8838412a5e014fbc46223b7e9a3f7495b24c.png)

That was my first design, but then I thought of a better positioning. All this was a pain to do, as I had to make sure everything was in line with the keyboard which is in a stupid 19.05 spacing.

![9237](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/f18095a666bb1dc8812195974658ec07e42efdb2ea0d67c0ed3c1c7ac0fed9e8.png)

## Finally got to routing

Manually routed things, with the intention of using dual ground pours. I think I only used 2 vias in the end. Was half considering adding support for another MCU at some point, by adding another set of pin headers to the board, but decided against it.

![9238](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/0d15909802f9df7446ad79f2ac8a1bd1ba8d67437507016787af7008f852848c.png)

And with the silkscreen and ground pour:

![9241](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/fec3f31b05e3244bdb44fcffa75610b01bec32857d08a87bd976a23727940462.png)

So, it was as easy as that - only took a full day to do (well kinda did start the first journals research yesterday as I had some ideas)

So I rendered the board out, and downloaded the Gerber and looked at the initial expected price

![9240](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/06d322bf1eb523a38bad11287c405d77f558ce1fcd066f37b6f203fc85e36e24.png)

![9242](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/b56ece937377036a99a62550aa76012a0a6a4d3f4d332da76f811754e0dedfca.png)

another photo (or 2) as it looks sick:

![9239](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/6aff67162415c601623e6c9ea789502bd01ecec85ac49e22cd4007c76b9ce82f.png)

![9241](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/fec3f31b05e3244bdb44fcffa75610b01bec32857d08a87bd976a23727940462.png)

### 2026-10-20 – # Started the case, and changed the PCB

**5.9h**

# Started the case, and changed the PCB

So I was bored last night, and decided to 3d model a case, as I'd finished the PCB all on the first day of the week.

So I exported the PCB SVG from Easyeda, to import into Fusion

![9591](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/2d6aee628b1524756084df29b7ea0de969f363b909a3a2826e56a4cfb2748c54.png)

This just gave me an "accurate" reference that I could model off.

So, I started modelling, parametrically of course, and then I found out that the svg I imported was the wrong dimensions. That was annoying.

![9244](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/aa4fce0286c33720a0aec7ce8492bca1564c6e944ba235ab4abe7d99f1a9dc93.png)

![9245](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/46d86244e004ceceea7a0a373a5255095465524c337bd03fea60a273c69acfbb.png)

And as you can't change a sketch to reimport an SVG, I had to start again from scratch. Which took too long. And I also only found out it was the wrong size when I was making the spacing for the keyboard switches - quite far in to making the case.

Realised I had a better photo of the problem:

![9246](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/2756d514f894f2749bcf1a488edfb4cd16cebe60488b78cae3793556737dc7b7.png)

But I did get it sorted in the end.

I also then had the problem of deciding how thick to make the walls. As for a keyboard switch panel, from my research, the average thickness is 1.5mm. Which to me seemed too thin for a 3d print. So I made a design, which went to 1.5mm where the switches snapped in, but then tapered thicker in the middle.

And I also spent a good while figuring out how I wanted to make the case. As in how many seperate pieces I would need. I knew I needed one for the switch panel, but I wanted to see if I could get away with just having that. so I made a lip on the inside which the PCB could get pushed up into, and then added some holes for threaded inserts which I can then use to screw the PCB in place. I also only added these to the back, as the switches should hold it up at the front, and I also dont have the space without making the case huge - it's currently only about a cm thick, and I think is like 10x8cm. So probably too compact.

If I do it again, will make it less compact, so I could both design it, and later on, build and assemble it quicker.

Then, I found out you can export a 3d model from Easyeda. So I exported it the switches and the rp2040, and realised I had a few problems.

First of all, I couldn't make the panel any thicker, but also, the rp2040 zero would hit the top panel

![9247](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/4af292237e987afc419eb120a16ab42dbfa59a50ccd3265f7eb3c9d15167e4e7.png)

So firstly, I just decided to make the panel 1.5mm thick, which meant I'd have to get it printed out of some strong, but expensive material. From research mabye metal or something.

And I also decided that instead of rewiring the board, I'll just surface mount the rp2040. So I looked into doing that, then realised I had a few vias under the board. Had to get rid of those, otherwise they might cause problems.

So I rewired the board by hand, making sure there were no vias underneath the board

![9249](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/192beb6820ccd405a6936411f34ce1beb77a268b26812d7207b92766b6298e05.png)

Then it was rather late, so I decided to come back to it the day after (will most likely get it done today - benefits of being on holiday - except I won't be at my computer for the last half of the week).

## tl:dr

SVG's in Fusion 360 can have the wrong scale. And are a pain to resize. Had to remodel the case for that. Part tolerances and clearances also are important. had to reroute the board for that.

### 2026-10-20 – # Finished the Case

**7.4h**

# Finished the Case

Spent a while experimenting with different sole heights, and positionings, with no raised lip etc, slope angle as well. Finally decided to have it raised up by 6mm to allow for the keys, then had the slope go at a 20 degree angle in the end. possibly too shallow, but we'll have to see.

That's one version:

![9250](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/5b046dc3eeed03135b16cc898e5caec17d1d3cc21bf6e0c138bf15938a342a3c.png)

This is the latest one:

![9251](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/7828e117307a08dfbb8a9c72614eb691dcbc77c971eef8ab915abc553c1d8af9.png)

So after that, I realised that I gave myself very little space to work with, in that I had no clue how I'd arranged things inside the case. So I decided to make a reference model of the screen.

This was a slight pain as the 0.91 oled I went for, is commonly confused with the 0.96 oled, and the datasheets had different values.

![9657](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/1173c8759e0bbdfb7656737af922bef9f9a62a12ce114b3234d7b9dddcc64800.png)

So I did model one off these dimensions, and it looked alright, except it was sort of meh. Like I wasn't quite sure if all the dimensions were quite right etc. So in the end, I just spent another half an hour looking for designs on the internet. And in the end, I found this really good site called Grab cad, which I got a step model off, so I'm hoping that's accurate enough.

![9252](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/165006cc807c3171f31fcda302eabbdda4a753d3d22222af71f462d0de3b7e8a.png)

Then I figured out the actual screen size within the black bit, centered it in the slope - I hope this is right, instead of shifted up or down - then made a cutout for it, and a relief for the PCB. This became a problem later though.

![9253](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/6276e8a95c9b996ebbc7380fcec6bdd600b27c30875957da111f4a3ea7fbd487.png)

Originally I was planning to make reference models for the encoders as well, but I decided just to run with it, and check measurements by hand (probably a bad idea). So I had to go back to AliExpress to look for knobs, and ended up with these:

![9254](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/dc1bcd35149f631a3e661c1f568b906c5cbb4657f795fbdaf4423f29f21e0553.png)

It was all a surprising pain to do, as when looking up the metal knobs I wanted, I got a lot of expensive ones, a lot of too large ones, and a lot of guitar knobs.

But anyway, so I placed the holes centered horizontally on the slopes bit, then guessed a position for the centers until they looked good. A highly scientific way might I add.

That got me this:

![9257](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/991d917ec3b50a1760c7a3cb080d1d457f51c53ee75beb7f50eb0a55c671d77b.png)

So I uploaded it to jlc3dp, and got a warning. In my intelligence, I made the relief for the screen a whole 0.2mm thick. Not really sure how I managed this, but meant I had to go back and change things.

So it's now 0.75mm thick at it's thinnest point, and whilst I was at it, I spent way too long beefing the rest of the sides up to at least 1.5mm - visible in the section analysis below:

![9256](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/fe04df7b6e8e0033c17655475a48185b8264867b214871832660edcf663e9985.png)

And with that, I was done. Well aside from adding mounting hardware, power cutouts etc - all thing that seems small but took a fair bit of time - especially the usbc port on the rp2040. Who knows you need to make them square for some clunky cables?

But anyway, I got around to ordering for the second time, and this time there was only a yellow warning for thinness. Hopefully it will be fine.

![9258](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/cf748d456f524d5d0a771f8e3842c75d602bd89d36feaf8ce8b50cb1c4feaa39.png)

 Oh and I also decided to get it made out of MJF nylon. As from research it is meant to be really strong and durable.

## Other notes
Just for the record, I thought of this before the starter project was announced, although they are quite similar. However because of the starter project, I'm not going to include a speaker built in, but will probably get one to connect to it, as somehow, I don't actually have any speakers (literally just got my phone and earbuds).

Oh and I'm also planning to make 2 of these. One for each hand.

## tl;dr
Spent way too long messing with slop positioning and angles, as well as reference pieces. Eventually got it finished, and it's looking pretty good
